title: Cheesy Chicken Broccoli Rice
seoTitle: Cheesy Chicken Broccoli Rice | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: One-pot cheddar chicken and rice for ten
subtitle: One-pot cheddar chicken and rice for ten
description: Chicken breast cubes cook with rice and broccoli in one pot, then finish with sharp cheddar until creamy and cohesive. Simple seasoning, big portions, minimal dishes.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Cheesy Chicken Broccoli Rice in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.instruction: Season cubed chicken with salt, garlic powder, and onion powder. Sear in butter 4–5 minutes until lightly golden—not fully cooked through.

steps.title: Add rice and broth
steps.instruction: Stir in rice and onion, toast 1 minute, then pour in broth. Bring to boil, cover, reduce to low simmer. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Simmer covered
steps.instruction: Cook covered 18 minutes without lifting lid until rice absorbs liquid and chicken reaches 165°F internal. Target oven/smoker temperature: 165°F.

steps.title: Steam the broccoli
steps.instruction: Nestle broccoli on top, cover, and cook 8 more minutes until broccoli tender and rice fluffy. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Cheesy Chicken Broccoli Rice onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Finish with cheese
steps.instruction: Remove from heat, stir in cheddar and remaining butter until melted and creamy. Rest 5 minutes before serving. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Rotisserie chicken shredded in at the end skips the sear step on busy nights.
A teaspoon of mustard powder in the cheese adds depth without tasting like mustard.
Hot sauce on the table beats cooking spice into the whole pot.
tonightSpread: One-pot scoops with dinner rolls and simple mixed greens.
Extra shredded cheese at the line for crew who want it cheesier.
leftovers: Reheat with splash of broth in a covered pan on low.
Press cold leftovers into patties and pan-fry for crispy rice cakes.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Every hall has a version of this dish because it works. One pot, familiar flavors, and even rookies can follow the steps without burning the house down.
mealPrepNotes: Cut chicken uniform so it cooks with the rice. Add broccoli in the last 8 minutes so it stays green. Stir cheese off heat for smoothest melt.
